payload_by_class.note: Manufacturer: '1,000kg' LEO, '700kg' SSO. POLAR 800 kg = team assumption (between LEO and SSO; polar ~90° costs less than retrograde SSO ~97°).

ref_alt_km.note: Reference altitude of manufacturer figures assumed (standard SSO reference 500 km); not published.

max_alt_km.note: Max. orbit altitude for E1; no manufacturer figure found (website states no max. altitude).

isar_ramp.note: Ramp-up = capacity ceiling (cap), not a forecast flight count (ASTRA_AUDIT B1/P3). 2027/28 = company plan (4 flights 2027, doubling 2028, https://payloadspace.com/seops-books-five-launches-on-isars-spectrum-rocket/), 2029/30 team assumption, 2031–2035 team assumption (D-027): extrapolation up to factory capacity of 40/year (https://europeanspaceflight.com/isar-aerospace-announces-new-launch-date-alongside-series-d-funding/) as the ceiling; no entry from 2036, because the corridor has no E3 point values. In the 2030 base run the cap does not bind (Astra: 10.76 missions at cap 18). 2026 added (D-017): flight 2 reached orbit on 05.09.2026, at most one further launch in the rest of 2026 (team assumption). Plan v2 section 5. Factory target 'up to 40 rockets/year' is production capacity, not cadence. Manifest plausibility: 2028 'at least four flights' and 2028 manifest full (https://payloadspace.com/seops-books-five-launches-on-isars-spectrum-rocket/); SEOPS 5 dedicated launches 2028–2030 from Andøya and Nova Scotia (same source); Astroscale ADRAS-J2 2027/28 (https://isaraerospace.com/press/isar-aerospace-signs-launch-contract-with-astroscale-japan) and ELSA-M FY2028+ (https://isaraerospace.com/press/isar-aerospace-secures-first-active-debris-removal-mission-with-astroscale); NO AOS, ESA missions. Base 2028 = 8 is therefore on the optimistic side.

meta.note: Calendar years from first-flight year, orbital attempts only, excluding HASTE. Ramps are shape comparisons, not forecasts. Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence of demand, not an upper bound.

electron.name: Rocket Lab Electron
electron.note: research/historie.md §2, confidence high (cadence) / medium (price); 300 kg LEO / 200–300 kg SSO; years 2017–2024, 2025: 18 orbital flights; HASTE suborbital excluded. Failures: 1 of 10 (maiden flight 25.05.2017), further failures on flights 13 (04.07.2020), 20 (15.05.2021), 41 (19.09.2023). Price ~$7.5 million ≈ $25,000/kg (Feb 2020); secondary source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Lab_Electron. Use only the shape of the ramp, not the absolute number. Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence that demand exists, not an upper bound.

vega.name: Vega
vega.note: research/historie.md §2, confidence medium; 1,450 kg SSO 400 km; years 2012–2019. Failures: 0 of 10; first failure on flight 15 (VV15, 11.07.2019), second VV17 (17.11.2020). Price ~€32 million incl. services at 2 launches/yr (2012); $37 million (infobox); secondary source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_(rocket). Vega retired 05.09.2024 (22 flights, 2 failures). Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence that demand exists, not an upper bound.

alpha.name: Firefly Alpha
alpha.note: research/historie.md §2, confidence medium; 1,030 kg LEO / 630 kg SSO; years 2021–2026, 2026 only through Oct (incomplete). 7 flights: 2 failures (03.09.2021, 29.04.2025) + 2 partial successes (01.10.2022, 22.12.2023) = 29 % (57 %); return to flight FLTA007 12.03.2026 (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/03/firefly-flta007-launch/). Price $15–17.6 million (undated). Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence that demand exists, not an upper bound.

rockot.name: Rockot (Eurockot)
rockot.note: research/historie.md §2, confidence medium; 1,950 kg LEO / 1,200 kg SSO; count starts with the commercial Eurockot launch on 16.05.2000 (maiden flight from Baikonur 26.12.1994 not counted as year 1), years 2000–2007. Failures: 1 of 10 (CryoSat 08.10.2005); 34 flights in total, 2 failures, 1 partial; retired 26.12.2019. Price ~$15 million (1999); Swarm contract €27.1 million (2013); $41.8 million (infobox, undated). Converted-missile launcher: demand, not supply, was the cap. Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence that demand exists, not an upper bound.

pslv.name: PSLV
pslv.note: research/historie.md §2, confidence medium; 1,100–1,750 kg SSO 620 km depending on variant; years 1993–2000. Failures: 1 of 10 (maiden flight 20.09.1993) + 1 partial success (C1 1997) = 10 % (20 %); active, 63 flights through 12.01.2026, 4 failures, 1 partial. Price ₹130–200 crore ≈ $16–25 million (2023 equivalent); secondary source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle. State-owned launcher, 2–4× the class (historie.md: not suitable as an analogue, demand evidence only). Vega = institutional comparison, not a universal cap; Rockot = evidence that demand exists, not an upper bound.

isar.name: Isar Aerospace Spectrum
isar.note: 2026 to 21.10.2026; scenarios from assumptions.isar_ramp = capacity ceiling, not a flight forecast (ASTRA P3). Flight 1 30.03.2025 failure (~30 s), flight 2 05.09.2026 orbit. 1,000 kg LEO / 700 kg SSO.

rules.source: Day 2 brief (task 2): EO_OPTICAL (IMG), EO_RADAR (IMG-R), WEATHER_CLIMATE (MET, MET-RO, EOSCI), BROADBAND (COM + captive), IOT_M2M (COM not captive, < 100 kg), COMMS_OTHER, NAV, DEFENCE_ISR (SIG, EW, Class D with IMG), IN_ORBIT_SERVICES (TECH with debris/servicing; brief also listed demo, removed per D-021; Astroscale, ClearSpace, Dcubed), SCIENCE (SCI, AST, BIO, GEOD, MGRAV), EDUCATION (EDU, Class A), CREW_CARGO (SS), OTHER
rules.note: First matching rule wins. Class D with IMG/IMG-R before EO, so that military reconnaissance counts as DEFENCE_ISR. mass_max_kg in IOT_M2M must equal iot_max_kg (test). 'demo' from the brief deliberately NOT included (D-021): in the GCAT inventory all four demo hits were false matches (PHI-DEMO, SR-0 Demosat, Argonaut Demo, LM-400 Tech Demo); coverage and name list are in build_report.json (verticals).

default.note: Remainder (TECH without IOS keyword, CAL, RV, unknown).

meta.note: History 1957–2026: mass and launcher classes, structural breaks. from_year replaces assumptions.history.from_year (kept there as alias).

from_year.note: research/historie.md §1.1, confidence high; start of the GCAT series (Sputnik 1, 04.10.1957).

mass_classes.note: research/historie.md §1.1/§1.5 (Z5), confidence high (Mini/Small/≤1,200 kg) / medium (Nano/Micro thresholds from Bryce 2021: https://web1.brycetech.com/reports/report-documents/Bryce_Smallsats_2021.pdf, gap L7); bounds inclusive; mass < 1 kg -> NANO lower bound (pipeline rule); UNKNOWN if no mass.

lv_class_thresholds.note: research/historie.md §1.2, confidence high (Bryce) / medium (FAA compendium https://www.faa.gov/about/office_org/headquarters_offices/ast/media/Annual_Compendium_of_Commercial_Space_Transportation_2012_February_2013.pdf); SMALL < 2,268 kg LEO (Micro+Small), MEDIUM 2,268–11,340, HEAVY > 11,340; UNKNOWN if unassigned.

structural_breaks.note: research/historie.md §4, confidence high (direction); descriptive, no causal interpretation; break year excluded; n subsequent years 6 / 4 / 3 up to base_year 2025.

mcdowell_payload_mass_2025.note: Total payload mass 2025 per McDowell incl. Starship test ships and mass simulators; tool E0 excludes these (D-009), hence 2,707 t instead of 3,193 t.

bryce_smallsats_2025.note: Smallsats (<= 1,200 kg) launched in 2025; comparable to E0 count in scope smallsats_le_1200kg (tool: 4,474, difference due to launch failures/auxcat objects).

bryce_megaconstellation_share_2025.note: Share of LEO broadband megaconstellations in 2025 smallsat deployments, incl. OneWeb; the tool does not count OneWeb as captive (plan section 9); captive share of the 2025 E0 count in the tool: 77.5% (BROADBAND).

novaspace_eo_tripling.note: Novaspace expects EO satellites to triple 2024–2033 (5,401 sats); equivalent to ~11.6 %/year; tool base case EO 8 %/year.

isar_valuation_2026.note: >€2bn, attribution: transaction advisor Greenberg Traurig, 16.06.2026; Bloomberg ~€2bn (23.03.2026, via mezha.net); company has not disclosed; no FT source; confidence low. research/kapital.md §3, research/sonstiges.md §3.2, ASTRA_AUDIT.md P8.

isar_private_capital_total.note: ≈€820 million private capital 2019–2026, derived: >€400 million (as of 06/2024) + €150 million convertible bond (06/2025) + €270 million Series D (06/2026); Dealroom cites US$872 million. research/kapital.md §3, confidence medium (only “>400” as primary figure).
